name: Ashwall Fixer's Complete Underworld Set
description: A fixer's look is studied neutrality: mid-weight longcoat in slate-grey waxed synthwool, unbranded, cut wide enough to conceal hardware and accommodate a partial spinal rig. Beneath it, a structured collarless shirt in dark indigo — Yoruba-inspired block print barely visible in direct light — tucked into slim tapered trousers with concealed inner-thigh pockets. Footwear is a low-profile matte ankle boot, no metal hardware to trip scanners. Hands covered by thin grip-null gloves. A flat cap or structured hood — situationally deployed — completes the look. The whole outfit reads as Tier 3 from thirty meters and reveals nothing closer.
functionality: Concealed inner-thigh pockets; scanner-neutral boot hardware; longcoat cut accommodates spinal rig and concealed carry; grip-null gloves leave no biometric traces on surfaces; hood deployment takes under two seconds.
what_it_says: This person moves between worlds and belongs to none of them — which means they belong to whoever's paying.
manufacturer: Ashwall Independent (assembled from multiple unlicensed sources)
story_hooks: The block-print shirt is a specific pattern tied to a dissolved Lagos-corridor trade guild — wearing it is either a statement or a mistake.
The inner-thigh pocket contains a data chip that the wearer claims not to know the contents of.
Every piece of this outfit was purchased separately, in different districts, over eighteen months — someone built an identity that can't be traced to a single transaction.
